title: Constancy of the Speed of Light as a Theorem:  Why Only Dynamically Supported Spacetime Can Sustain a Finite Invariant Speed
content: In special relativity, the constancy of the speed of light \(c\) is introduced as a postulate.  Here we show that a finite invariant speed cannot be \emph{derived} within a  stage-only spacetime---one lacking dynamical substrate or causal microstructure.  Using the group-theoretic classification of kinematical symmetries and geometric  equivalence arguments, we demonstrate that the existence of a finite invariant  speed is \emph{mathematically equivalent} to endowing spacetime with a Lorentzian  conformal structure whose null cones define causal propagation.  Absent such a structure, the only self-consistent invariant is \(c=\infty\).  Hence, the constancy of \(c\) is not a mere consequence of symmetry but a manifestation  of an underlying causal dynamics. Chronon Field Theory (CFT) provides such a substrate:  its alignment field generates Lorentzian geometry and enforces a universal propagation  limit \(c_\Phi=\sqrt{J/\lambda}\) across all interactions.  The constancy and universality of \(c\) thus emerge as dynamical consequences  of causal coherence, transforming Einstein’s postulate into a theorem.
